note: AUTH-OPERATIONS-011: machine-readable mirror of docs/07 section 15.6's release-signoff checklist. Never edit an item's description here without updating the matching markdown checkbox in docs/07 (and vice versa) -- scripts/validate-release-checklist.mjs fails CI the moment the two diverge, in either direction. Filling in status/evidence for a real release is an operator's job; nothing in this repository or its CI can set status to "verified" on its own -- see AUTH-OPERATIONS-011's own canonical requirement text: production readiness must be an explicit machine-readable evidence checklist, 'never a certification or automatic security claim.' To mark an item verified, set status to "verified" and evidence to a structured object: {"verifiedBy": "<real operator identifier>", "verifiedAt": "<ISO 8601 timestamp, not in the future>", "notes": "<at least 15 characters describing what was actually checked>"} -- a bare string, an empty/placeholder value in any field, or a future timestamp fails validation just as hard as a stale item list does.

items.description: Release 1 Verification is green on final deployed code head

evidence.notes: Production (Vercel deployment dpl_ANkSN7nywoz7VMMPE44XG6q9LnJ1) is running commit 406596b5, and the Release 1 Verification GitHub Actions workflow run for that exact commit (run 33896757225, https://github.com/marceloATpixelsmith/idoc.club/actions/runs/33896757225) completed with conclusion success.

34 of 35 migrations recorded in idoc.__drizzle_migrations; the one gap (0007_account_delivery_token_eligibility) is a self-healed bookkeeping quirk, not a real schema gap: 0007's out-of-order timestamp caused the migrator to silently skip it, but 0008_reconcile_account_delivery_eligibility (which did run) adds the same terminal_at/terminal_reason columns via ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS. Confirmed both columns exist on idoc.account_delivery_outbox in production via information_schema.columns, and zero runtime errors on /api/cron/account-delivery in the last 7 days.

items.description: Required Production auth variables are configured in Vercel

evidence.notes: Operator visually confirmed every variable lib/runtime/configuration.ts fail-closed-requires is present in the Vercel Production environment: POSTGRES_URL, AUTH_SECRET, BASE_URL, CRON_SECRET, MAILCHIMP_TRANSACTIONAL_API_KEY, RATE_LIMIT_HASH_KEY, TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY, LOGIN_DEVICE_TRUST_DIGEST_KEY, MFA_TOTP_ACTIVE_KEY_ID, MFA_TOTP_ENCRYPTION_KEYS, MFA_PENDING_AUTH_SIGNING_KEY, MFA_RECOVERY_CODE_DIGEST_KEY, ACCOUNT_DELIVERY_KEY_VERSION, ACCOUNT_DELIVERY_ENCRYPTION_KEYS, IDOC_ADMIN_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY/WEBHOOK_SECRET/RECURRING_PRODUCT_ID/ONE_TIME_PRODUCT_ID, GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/REDIRECT_URI. Google's client secret is configured via the rotation-ready GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET_VERSIONS+_ACTIVE_VERSION pair (also present); confirmed in lib/auth/google-oidc-reference.ts that when VERSIONS is set it takes exclusive priority, so the also-present legacy GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET is inert, not a conflict.

Confirmed in Google Cloud Console's OAuth 2.0 Client credentials page: Authorized JavaScript origins list both https://idoc.club and https://redesign.idoc.club (the in-progress redesign's staging domain); Authorized redirect URIs list the matching https://idoc.club/api/auth/google/callback and https://redesign.idoc.club/api/auth/google/callback, exactly matching the app's real callback route and the GOOGLE_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI convention.

items.description: Security-email delivery and retry operation are verified

evidence.notes: Real production delivery confirmed by querying idoc.auth_security_notification_outbox: 4 real historical rows, all sent_at populated, including two authenticator_enrolled events from this session's own real TOTP re-enrollment tests. Retry behavior for account_delivery_outbox and operational_alert_outbox was already proven by real forced-failure integration tests; auth_security_notification_outbox had no equivalent (only a source-inspection-only test for an unrelated bug), so tests/auth-security-notification-delivery.integration.ts was added, forcing a real transient failure and a real dead-letter through the actual production deliverNextAuthSecurityNotification function against real Postgres (4/4 passing).
